HEADLINE: "Andy Burnham's Vow to Change UK Labour Already Risks Coming Unstuck"
DATED: 18 July 2026 (Saturday) — this is the clearest genuinely Saturday-dated UK politics
analysis piece located.

REPORTED CONTENT (UNVERIFIED EXTRACTS):
- Burnham becomes Britain's 59th PM on 20 July, confirmed as Labour leader on Friday 17 July.
- His transition into government has been "dominated by a policy vacuum, indecision in his
  inner circle, a high-profile falling out with one of his main allies and a nascent rebellion
  from Labour's left flank."
  => The identity of the ally is NOT given in any extract obtained. DO NOT NAME.
- Decentralisation defines Burnham's politics; he argues Britain is unusually centralised.
- His answer: the biggest transfer of power away from Whitehall in generations, handing regions
  control over transport, housing and adult education.
- Clearest symbol: "Number 10 North", a satellite operation based at a government digital
  campus near Manchester Piccadilly.
